html:
A Florentine official and writer whose book The Prince described how rulers win and keep power as it is really done, not as it ought to be.

After the Medici were driven out of Florence in 1494 and the preacher Savonarola fell, Machiavelli served the republic from 1498 to 1512 as secretary and envoy. He met Cesare Borgia and set up a citizen militia. When the Medici came back in 1512 he lost his post, was jailed and tortured, and retired to his farm.

There he wrote The Prince in 1513; it was printed only in 1532, after his death. He argued that a ruler must be ready to lie and to use cruelty when needed, and that if he cannot be both feared and loved, it is safer to be feared. He also wrote the Discourses on Livy, which praise republics.

"Machiavellian" came to mean cunning and ruthless, and the Church banned his books. But he is also seen as a founder of modern political science, which treats politics on its own terms. His world was the Italian Wars and the age of the Medici.
